The probe's finding of record this batch: vaultwarden's unauth surface is WIDER than previously recorded. Prior batches leaned on the 127.0.0.1:8062 host bind to call the unauth legs 'LAN/insider-scoped', but that bind only constrains the DIRECT container port — traefik_auth_modes.vaultwarden='oidc' attaches NO forward-auth middleware to the auto-published Host(`pass.<tld>`) router, so anonymous HTTPS transits the edge into the app over iiab_net/shared_net. Rated MEDIUM, not HIGH: SSRF is blind-ish and the WS leg is availability-only, SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=false, and no internet exposure unless the TLD is publicly routed. GENERAL LESSON for future native_oidc services: 'oidc' in traefik_auth_modes means the EDGE IS OPEN and the app's own login is the only gate — pre-auth endpoints (icons, websockets, health, well-known) of every native_oidc service are anonymously reachable and must be scored as such. attack_probe_schedule.name: version_header_leakage

attack_probe_schedule.note: Cycle-25 batch-48 SECOND RUN of this probe type, over mariadb/redis/infisical/rustfs/qgis_server (2026-08-10), completing the batch-47 attempt that died at write-back. 2 items filed (REM-189, REM-190, both MEDIUM, both rustfs). THE PROBE'S FINDING OF RECORD: fs.pazny.eu/health returns 200 anonymously with the exact string "version":"1.0.0-beta.11", and internet reach was PROVEN rather than assumed -- the request was re-issued against the public Cloudflare anycast address and came back with server: cloudflare, cf-ray ...-PRG and cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC, i.e. through the real edge to this origin, uncached. That is the evidentiary standard REM-144 explicitly could not meet (split-horizon dnsmasq had resolved its 'public' test back to the LAN, so it correctly refused to claim internet exposure); future probes should reach for --resolve against the authoritative public address before either claiming or disclaiming reach. It also overturns the 'pre-auth leg is CLOSED' disposition rustfs had carried since batch-36 -- the leg is not closed, it is narrowed to /health and /favicon.ico, and /health is the one that talks. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is about TIME rather than about headers: an advisory verdict is only true as of the hour it was read. REM-187 recorded rustfs's advisory leg clean at 04:12 and predicted, from this vendor's demonstrated habit of retroactively naming later releases as sole-patched, that beta.11 would likely acquire advisories anyway. Six were published at 14:13 the same day -- four against beta.11 and two against beta.12, the very version REM-187 recommended bumping TO. The prediction was right within ten hours, which means for a no-CVE prerelease vendor a clean verdict must carry its timestamp and a short shelf life. Pair that with the version disclosure above and the two findings compose: the estate publishes, anonymously and worldwide, exactly the string an attacker needs to know when this host's version enters an affected range. SECONDARY PATTERN, the probe's nominal quarry across all five: the components with NO HTTP surface are not automatically silent. MariaDB's pre-auth MySQL handshake advertises '11.8.8-MariaDB-ubu2404' -- application version AND Ubuntu base image -- to anyone who can open a socket, which is protocol-inherent and unfixable by config; Redis under --requirepass answers '-NOAUTH Authentication required.' to INFO, PING and LOLWUT alike and discloses nothing, a protocol-design difference rather than a configuration one. Neither is filed (both are loopback-bound with no router), but the sidecar observation is worth carrying: redis_exporter republishes redis_version="8.10.0" on an unauthenticated /metrics, so an exporter can undo the reticence its service carefully maintains. And qgis_server returns `Server: Apache/2.4.18 (Ubuntu)` -- one header fingerprinting a 2019 Ubuntu 16.04 userland -- which is not a new row but is the cleanest possible evidence for REM-184; it does not reach the internet only because REM-185's missing Authentik Provider makes the edge 404 first. --- PRIOR: Cycle-17 batch-38 FIRST RUN of this probe type, over woodpecker/jellyfin/traefik/uptime_kuma/calibreweb (2026-07-30): 4 items (REM-144 CRITICAL, REM-145 HIGH, REM-146 LOW, REM-147 LOW) + REM-148. Looking for leaked version strings surfaced leaked CREDENTIALS -- Traefik's dashboard/API answered anonymously at the edge because traefik_auth_modes.traefik='none', and /api/http/middlewares served rendered customRequestHeaders verbatim, disclosing X-Wing-Edge-Token, X-Face-Edge-Token and global_password_prefix itself. Lesson recorded there: 'oidc' means the edge is open and the app's own login is the only gate; 'none' means there is no gate at all. Also: security-headers@file strips NO response headers, it only adds, so any upstream Server or X-Powered-By passes through the edge untouched.

attack_probe_schedule.note: Cycle-34 batch-56 SECOND run of this probe type, over nginx,vaultwarden,ollama,mailpit,spacetimedb (2026-08-20). 2 items filed (REM-210 vaultwarden MEDIUM, REM-211 mailpit MEDIUM) + REM-172 (ollama) CLOSED by measurement. THE PROBE'S FINDING OF RECORD IS AN INVERSION OF ITS OWN FIRST RUN, and it is the rule this probe type should carry forward: DO NOT STOP WHEN THE CREDENTIAL TURNS OUT TO BE STRONG. Batch-49 filed superset and freescout as HIGH because the gate was a guessable prefix-derived string. Vaultwarden declares the IDENTICAL prefix-derived template (default.credentials.yml:411) and is not vulnerable to it -- main.yml:1494 intercepts any '_pw_' value and mints 48 random bytes, verified in the running container (ADMIN_TOKEN len 64, random head) and backed by a MEASURED rate limit (6 wrong-token POSTs -> 401,401,401,429,429,429). A probe that grepped for prefix-derived values would have called it clean and stopped. The row exists because the real question is HOW MANY INDEPENDENT FACTORS stand between the internet and an admin capability, and at https://pass.pazny.eu/admin the answer is one: HTTP 200 anonymously through the real Cloudflare edge (--resolve 188.114.96.9, cf-ray ...-PRG, DYNAMIC), a rendered Traefik router with no authentik@file, a panel that bypasses Authentik entirely and displays live SMTP credentials, and a token upstream itself logs as plain-text on every boot. SECOND PATTERN, one step further out: A CONTROL CAN BE ABSENT BY CONDITIONAL. mailpit's MP_UI_AUTH renders only inside `{% if mailpit_ui_user | length > 0 %}` and NOTHING in the repo ever sets mailpit_ui_user -- three grep hits repo-wide, two defaults and the reader, zero setters. The guard has never once been true, so a control that reads as configured has never existed, and the mail archive (every password-reset link and invitation token the estate has sent) is unauthenticated to every peer container on the flat net. That is CLAUDE.md's success-marker class in a new surface: the code that would have to configure the control is also the code asserting it. Gate opportunity: walk every `{% if <var> | length > 0 %}` in the compose templates and assert <var> has at least one non-empty assignment somewhere. THIRD, on evidence standards: the components with no credential mechanism are not automatically silent, but here they genuinely were -- ollama has no auth by design (upstream's own GHSA-f6mr-38g8-39rg) so its loopback bind IS the access control, and that was verified with lsof (127.0.0.1:11434 LISTEN, IPv4 only) rather than read off a plist; spacetimedb mints its JWT keypair per host with openssl at 0600 and ships no admin account; nginx has never shipped an auth_basic realm anywhere in the repo (zero grep hits). --- PRIOR: Cycle-26 batch-49 FIRST run over superset,outline,freescout,paperclip,tileserver. Finding of record: 'oidc' in traefik_auth_modes = edge OPEN + app login is the only gate, and for superset (REM-191) and freescout (REM-192) that gate is a prefix-derived default credential -- both internet-reachable. +REM-193 (freescout currency). outline/paperclip/tileserver have no local-credential surface.
